aldermanic-incomplete-filings.area: Kaukauna, Bellevue, Berlin, Brillion, Cuba City, Durand, Edgerton, New London, Port Washington
aldermanic-incomplete-filings.summary: Nine cities and villages have no aldermanic districts on the map because their counties' ward filings leave some or most wards unassigned, so their district lines cannot be drawn honestly.
aldermanic-incomplete-filings.why: The districts are unions of wards, and the state's ward file is only as complete as each county's filing. Where a filing codes a fraction of a city's wards, drawing just that fraction would show fragments as if they were the whole plan.
aldermanic-incomplete-filings.wanted: For one of the nine: a county ward filing that assigns every city ward its district, the city's own boundary file, or a city page naming the wards in each district. Kaukauna is the largest of the nine.

alderperson-rosters.summary: In most of the 156 municipalities with districts on the map, the card names your district but not the council member holding it. Eighteen name their alderpersons or trustees; the rest link nothing yet.
alderperson-rosters.why: Wisconsin has no open statewide roster of municipal council members — the league sells one to non-members on terms it calls exclusive use — so each roster is read from the city's own site, and seventeen sites refuse automated readers.
alderperson-rosters.wanted: For any city or village with districts on the map: a page pairing each aldermanic or trustee district with the member holding it, readable without a sign-in. A statewide open roster of municipal officials would close this gap wholesale.

french-island-census-lag.area: Village of French Island (La Crosse County) — the former Town of Campbell
french-island-census-lag.summary: On French Island the map gives three answers to one question: the ward card says Village of French Island, the County Subdivision card says Campbell town, and the City or Village card says the point is in no city or village at all.
french-island-census-lag.why: Those cards read different publishers. The ward layer is the state's, and it carries the village; the two municipal layers are the Census Bureau's, and TIGER still carries the territory as a town under its former name.
french-island-census-lag.wanted: The Census Bureau carrying the Village of French Island in TIGER's county-subdivision and Places layers. Nothing is needed from La Crosse County or the state — both already publish it correctly.

madison-tid-undrawn.summary: One of Madison's fifteen active tax districts is missing from the map — the state certified TID 55 as active in 2025, but the city has not yet published its boundary, so a reader inside it is told they are in no TID.
madison-tid-undrawn.why: The card can only draw what the city publishes as geometry. The state's certified active list and the city's own TIF program page both carry the district; the city's boundary layer does not yet.
madison-tid-undrawn.wanted: TID 55's boundary in the city's open-data TIF layer — the next operator rebuild ships it the moment it appears, and the builder's pin guarantees the change gets a human look.

municipal-officers.summary: Every Wisconsin municipality now names its clerk — towns on the County Subdivision card, cities and villages on their own. Nineteen Milwaukee County municipalities name their mayor or president too. None names its council or town board.
municipal-officers.why: The state aggregates just one municipal officer, the clerk, through the Elections Commission. No open roster of mayors, presidents, council or town board members exists; the league sells one to non-members, on terms it calls exclusive use.
municipal-officers.wanted: A statewide list pairing each municipality with its governing body — town board, village board or council. Short of that, another county publishing its executives, or a municipality's own page naming its officers.

ng911-ems-filings.area: Iowa, Jefferson, Langlade, Vilas and Walworth counties
ng911-ems-filings.summary: In five counties the EMS card can name no service, because their 911 authorities' EMS-boundary filings are absent from the state's NG911 aggregate.
ng911-ems-filings.why: The statewide layer is the Office of Emergency Communications' aggregate of each county 911 authority's own filing, and it can only carry what a county files — no other statewide publisher of who-is-dispatched-here boundaries exists.
ng911-ems-filings.wanted: The missing counties' EMS-boundary filings reaching the OEC aggregate — the state's roughly weekly refresh carries them the moment a county files.

ng911-law-filings.area: Iowa, Langlade, Vilas and Walworth counties, plus part of Polk
ng911-law-filings.summary: In four counties the law-enforcement card can name no agency, and in part of Polk County only some agencies, because those 911 authorities' law-boundary filings are absent or partial in the state's NG911 aggregate.
ng911-law-filings.why: The statewide layer is the Office of Emergency Communications' aggregate of each county 911 authority's own filing, and it can only carry what a county files — no other statewide publisher of who-serves-here boundaries exists.
ng911-law-filings.wanted: The missing or completed law-boundary filings reaching the OEC aggregate — the state's roughly weekly refresh carries them the moment a county files.

ward-polling-places.area: 29 wards in 12 municipalities — De Pere, Chippewa Falls, Amery, Wautoma, Dousman, River Falls, the Village of Summit, the Village of Lac La Belle, the Towns of Harrison, Fountain Prairie and Oshkosh
ward-polling-places.summary: The ward card names your polling place almost everywhere in Wisconsin, but 29 wards in 12 municipalities are missing from the state's own list, so those cards fall back to the MyVote lookup.
ward-polling-places.why: Each municipality assigns its own polling places and reports them to the Wisconsin Elections Commission, whose list the app ships. Where a ward the state's boundary file carries has no row in that list, there is nothing to pair it with.
ward-polling-places.wanted: Rows in the Commission's polling-place file for the 12 municipalities and 29 wards above — most likely arriving with the final November edition around 17 September 2026, which this project re-pulls either way.
